source.author: verg
source.text: Tum variae comitum facies, immania cete, et senior Glauci chorus, Inousque Palaemon, Tritonesque citi, Phorcique exercitus omnis; laeva tenent Thetis, et Melite, Panopeaque virgo, Nisaee, Spioque, Thaliaque, Cymodoceque.
source.text_original: Tum variae comitum facies, immania cete, / et senior Glauci chorus, Inousque Palaemon, / Tritonesque citi, Phorcique exercitus omnis; / laeva tenent Thetis, et Melite, Panopeaque virgo, / Nisaee, Spioque, Thaliaque, Cymodoceque.
source.text_english: Then the varied shapes of the attendants, huge whales, and old Glaucus’ band, Ino’s Palaemon, and the swift Tritons, and the whole army of Phorcus; on the left hold Thetis, and Melite, and the maiden Panopea, Nisaee, and Spio, and Thalia, and Cymodoce.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: hinc laevom Telamon pelagus tenet, altior inde occupat Alcides aliud mare, cetera pubes dividitur: celer Asterion, quem matre cadentem Piresius gemino fovit pater amne Cometes, segnior Apidani vires ubi sentit Enipeus.
reuse.text_original: hinc laevom Telamon pelagus tenet, altior inde / occupat Alcides aliud mare, cetera pubes / dividitur: celer Asterion, quem matre cadentem / Piresius gemino fovit pater amne Cometes, / segnior Apidani vires ubi sentit Enipeus.
reuse.text_english: From here Telamon holds the sea to the left; from there Alcides occupies the other sea from a higher place. The rest of the young men are divided: swift Asterion, whom Piresius, his father, as he was falling, nourished with twin rivers, and slower Enipeus, where he feels the strength of the Apidanus.
